title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase: $4.56 (+5.1%) vs regular $4.34
drivers.evidence: Two prior weeks at $4.56: 2026-09-28 (x0.94), 2026-10-05 (x0.57). Both below baseline. Noise-adjusted price effect shrunk to x0.75 for limited data and high volatility. No prior promotion at this price, so no lift.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.6. A 5.1% price increase to $4.56 (from $4.34) is a known demand-reducing driver. Past data shows no promotion at this price point, but a prior week with $4.56 (2026-09-28) sold 195 units (x0.94 vs baseline), and the following week (2026-10-05) sold only 119 (x0.57). This suggests a strong negative price effect. The noise-adjusted price effect is shrunk toward 1.0 due to limited data (only two occurrences), but the consistent drop confirms a downward impact. No events or promotions are planned. The classical uplift model’s 1.00 is incorrect—this is not a typical week. The price rise likely reduces demand by ~25%–30%. Shrink effect to x0.75 for confidence. Downside spread increases due to uncertainty in the magnitude.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 4.56 (+5.1% vs regular price 4.34)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.6 | 5%-95%: 133.4 - 290.4 | 10%-90%: 156.2 - 281.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-22% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
